subject: Leadership pulse: scope trims, runway asks, and QBR artifacts
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Tara Scott <tara@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Leadership pulse: scope trims, runway asks, QBR artifacts

Team —

Quick mid-cycle pulse and a few asks as we prep the QBR. I tried to keep this tight so we can surface tradeoffs quickly. High level: we are behind on two measurable KR tracks (LLM throughput optimizations & telemetry coverage) and need to decide what to deprioritize so the rest can land with confidence.

Snapshot (short):
- KR: 30% reduction in per-token cost — status: 55% to target; blockers: quantization regression on safety net models.
- KR: 99.95% inference availability for Hosted tier — status: on track for infra but dependent on autoscaler change (infra work).
- KR: End-to-end QBR artifacts (customer-facing slides + runway model) — status: draft in Drive.

Proposed course-correct (asks):
1) Scope trim: push nonessential profiling tasks (detailed op-level tracing) to backlog for this cycle. This frees 2 FTE-weeks and avoids risk to the planned roll. Ask: PRiyom, confirm we can reallocate the profiling tickets.
2) Dependency ownership: the autoscaler change for hosted SLOs is the single largest risk. Vivek, request you to prioritize the autoscaler patch and surface cost impact if we move Dedicated routing as a fallback.
3) Customer alignment: ask Naomi to add a single-slide summary to the QBR deck highlighting the mitigation plan and expected timeline; also to loop Tara at Acme to set expectations on delivery.

Attachments: QBR-pulse-slides-v1.pdf, runway-modeling.xlsx (draft). Drive folder link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR-PULSE-REDWOOD-ACME

Timeline: need decisions EOD Wed (Aug 18) so the QBR narrative is stable.

Thanks —Kim

--
Kimberly Park
VP, Platform Programs | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
(attachment stub: QBR-pulse-slides-v1.pdf)
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Leadership pulse: scope trims, runway asks, QBR artifacts

Kim — thanks for the clear note. I agree with trimming the op-level tracing for this cycle; that buys us breathing room. Quick responses inline: 

- Profiling tickets: can move to backlog; I will reassign profiling-ops (PR-873) to backlog and move the bench-run tickets to next sprint. Owner: me. ETA: Tue EOD for updated tickets.
- Autoscaler change: I assessed the infra-side diff; it requires a small schema migration and a minor rollout gating change. If Vivek prioritizes, I estimate a 3-day turnaround to a canary. Dependencies: need a signed-off smoke test and the updated rollout policy (doc attached).

I've attached a slimmed risk doc (dependency-risks.docx) with the list of customers affected by a delayed autoscaler and suggested rollback points. Also flagging we may need a short burst of Dedicated capacity (~2wks) if the canary needs more stable capacity.

Action items I will own: update tickets + create a one-pager that lists what we trim and what stays.

--
Priyom Das
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
(attachment stub: dependency-risks.docx)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Leadership pulse: scope trims, runway asks, QBR artifacts

Appreciate the framing. Quick infrastructure reality check: our Hosted autoscaler change is straightforward code-wise but our current GPU cluster utilization for this region is high (we're at ~88% steady-state with queued batch traffic peaks). If we try to push the canary into the same pool we risk noisy neighbor impact. Two options:

A) Fast path: provision temporary Dedicated capacity for the canary (approx cost estimate: $18k for 2 weeks) and perform the autoscaler rollout there.
B) Conservative path: throttle batch pipelines for a 48–72 hour window during canary which may affect internal batch SLAs.

I recommend option A to keep customer-facing latency stable through the QBR period; I'll start the procurement request if leadership signs off. Raising JIRA-RED-4592 and JIRA-RED-4620 for the autoscaler rollout + procurement respectively.

If leadership is not comfortable with the cost, we can do B but we need clear acceptance criteria from the product owners.

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Infra & Ops
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Leadership pulse: scope trims, runway asks, QBR artifacts

Thanks — useful tradeoffs here. A few leadership notes: 

1) Narrative: The QBR cannot have ambiguity on customer impact. Kimberly, please add a single slide that summarizes the mitigation plan (autoscaler canary + temporary Dedicated routing fallback) and the decision we need from the execs (approve up to $20k temporary capacity).
2) Customer comms: please have Tara (Acme) on a 10-minute sync to confirm expectations; we should not surprise them with a scope change. Tara, are you available Wed 11:00–11:30 PT?
3) Finance: Aditya, flagging you to prep a quick approval path for a one-off Dedicated burst purchase if needed.

If we can get the decision by Wed EOD, we can keep the QBR narrative clean.

--
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Success
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Leadership pulse: scope trims, runway asks, QBR artifacts

Thanks all — quick confirmation and next steps below (closing the loop):

Decisions:
- We will trim op-level tracing for this cycle (Priyom to update tickets).
- Approve temporary Dedicated burst up to $20k for the canary (Vivek to start procurement request; Aditya, please stand by for fast-track approval).
- Naomi to run the 10-min sync with Tara Wed 11:00 PT (Tara, thanks for the quick availability).

Owners & deadlines:
- Priyom: move profiling tickets to backlog + one-pager by Tue EOD (Aug 17) (UPDATE: Priyom confirmed in-thread).
- Vivek: open procurement JIRA and schedule canary run; aim for canary by Thu (Aug 19). JIRA references: JIRA-RED-4592, JIRA-RED-4620.
- Naomi: customer sync Wed 11:00 PT; add 1-slide mitigation to QBR deck by Wed noon.
- Kimberly: finalize QBR deck v1 and circulate to execs by Thu morning.

I'll post the updated slide in the Drive folder (link above) and mark the files with v2 when done. Thanks for the quick responses — this keeps the QBR crisp and avoids late surprises.

Best —Kim
